races.paceDynamic: Dunkeld Dreamer will likely take the field along from the front, with Secret Force and No Knee Never providing company in the early stages. The presence of just these three prominent runners against six hold-up horses suggests a moderate early gallop that could quicken significantly in the home straight. With the majority of the field needing to be produced late, this creates a scenario where the early leaders may get first run but face sustained pressure from multiple closers. This race shape strongly favours horses with early tactical speed who can avoid the traffic problems that will inevitably develop when six hold-up horses try to make their moves simultaneously.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front runners prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Dunkeld Dreamer and Secret Force maintain strong early positions without over-racing
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace allows the leaders to conserve energy while the hold-up brigade gets shuffled back in the large field. When the closers make their moves, the front pair have enough left to resist, benefiting from clear racing room.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late closers swamp leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too slow and the hold-up horses get perfect splits
scenarios.body: The patient tactics pay dividends as multiple closers converge with telling late runs that overwhelm the tiring leaders. The higher-rated horses from the rear demonstrate superior class when it matters.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic chaos benefits handy
scenarios.trigger: If the large field creates significant interference problems in the straight for the hold-up horses
scenarios.body: Several of the six hold-up runners get checked or blocked at crucial moments, allowing the handily-placed runners to capitalize. Those positioned just behind the leaders avoid the worst of the scrimmaging.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Class rises to surface
scenarios.trigger: If the going deteriorates slightly or the pace becomes truly attritional
scenarios.body: The higher-rated horses Prince Of The Seas and Arqoob demonstrate their superior ability in testing conditions. Their class advantage becomes decisive when the race develops into a true staying test.

races.paceDynamic: Yanifer stands as the only confirmed front runner in this 22-runner handicap, likely to get an uncontested lead alongside prominent racers Mirabeau, Sujet, and Brighton Boy who may track close but won't challenge for the early lead. The sustainable early gallop will set up a tactical affair where positioning becomes crucial, with the large field creating traffic problems for those held up. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can sit handy, as the lack of early pace pressure means horses stuck at the back in this big field will struggle to make up ground when the sprint develops.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses get perfect positioning behind Yanifer's uncontested lead
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows handy horses to conserve energy and strike when ready, while hold-up horses get caught in traffic. Mirabeau, Brighton Boy, and Extremely Zain can all position ideally and have the class to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Navigates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the talented hold-up horses finds clear running through the big field
scenarios.body: Darkness or Akkadian Thunder uses their class advantage to weave through, benefiting from the sustainable pace that leaves something in the tank for a late charge. The pace scenario suits their style if they avoid trouble.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If Yanifer's soft lead proves insurmountable and no one can reel her in
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows Yanifer to dictate completely and find another gear when challenged, similar to her recent course success. Her 252-day break becomes irrelevant with this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the sustainable tempo becomes crawling slow and turns into a cavalry charge
scenarios.body: The big field bunches up completely creating a messy sprint finish where any horse with a clear run can win. Lower-rated horses with fresh conditions get their chance in the melee.

races.paceDynamic: Al Qareem emerges as the sole confirmed front runner in this six-runner Listed event, likely to dictate terms from the outset without serious early pressure. With all other runners showing prominent tendencies rather than genuine pace-pressing styles, Al Qareem can settle into a comfortable rhythm through the early stages of this 1m6f contest. The lack of genuine speed will create a moderate tempo that builds gradually, particularly through York's demanding home straight. This pace setup clearly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed, as the sustainable early gallop will leave plenty in reserve for the business end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Al Qareem dictates uncontested fractions through halfway
scenarios.body: The seven-year-old can control the tempo to suit his stamina reserves, making his class advantage tell in the final two furlongs when others struggle to quicken off the steady pace. His recent Ascot third behind smart opposition suggests he retains enough ability to exploit this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B

scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens meaningfully from the three-furlong pole
scenarios.body: Mount Atlas and Epic Poet can utilise their proven finishing kicks to reel in Al Qareem's advantage, with both showing strong recent placed efforts that indicate current wellbeing. The moderate early tempo will suit their style of racing just off the pace before striking late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Gregory Comeback Special
scenarios.trigger: If Gregory shows no signs of his 476-day absence affecting his fitness
scenarios.body: The Gosden-trained four-year-old possesses the highest class ceiling in this field and James Doyle's booking suggests strong stable confidence despite the lengthy layoff. His previous Group-level form would be superior to these opponents if he returns anywhere near his best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Roaring Legend Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses into a sprint finish favouring his decent turn of foot
scenarios.body: The lowest-rated runner could benefit from a truly-run race that plays to his stamina strengths, particularly given Olly Murphy's 32% strike-rate with his runners over the past fortnight. His recent placed efforts in staying handicaps suggest he handles this trip well when the pace is genuine.

races.paceDynamic: Five Ways will likely lead from the gates with limited early pressure in this large field sprint. The majority of runners are prominent racers who will settle just behind the leader, creating a bunched field through the early stages. With no confirmed pace antagonists, Five Ways can dictate terms and potentially steal crucial lengths turning for home before the cavalry charge begins. This tactical setup strongly favours front-running and prominent racers who can avoid traffic problems, while hold-up horses face the nightmare scenario of finding gaps in a 22-runner sprint with modest early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Five Ways gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear early in the straight
scenarios.body: The favourite can dictate his own fractions and prove hard to peg back when the field fan out late. Prominent racers with tactical speed will benefit from the clean run this creates.

scenarios.label: B

scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens from halfway as multiple prominent runners challenge Five Ways
scenarios.body: The increased tempo will set up a finish where horses with early positioning can quicken off a solid gallop. Those able to travel strongly into the straight will have the edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Nightmare
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady and the field remains bunched turning for home
scenarios.body: Traffic problems will be severe in the straight as 20+ horses look for racing room simultaneously. Only the most skilled jockeys will thread their horses through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Five Ways goes too slow early and gets swamped by the field at the two-furlong pole
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy cavalry charge where track position and luck matter more than ability. Horses drawn wide or with room to manoeuvre will have advantages.
